# Overview

This page performs the initial cleaning and reshaping of the baseline
couple interaction warmth data, ahead of the second-by-second synchrony
calculation carried out on [Baseline Synchrony
Calculation](Baseline-Synchrony_Calculation.qmd). Four steps happen
here:

1.  the raw wide-format SPSS export (one row per couple, one column per
    second) is reshaped into long format (one row per couple-second);
2.  missing-value codes are recoded to `NA`;
3.  the data is split into separate negative- and positive-discussion
    long datasets, one row per person per second; and
4.  warmth trajectories over time are plotted, both for the full sample
    and a representative subset in [Panel Plots].

# Data Cleaning

**Load Packages**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(here)
library(nlme)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2) 
library(lavaan)
library(semTools)
library(jtools)
library(haven)
library(modsem)
library(forecast)
library(gt)
```
:::






## Transformation

The raw file has one row per couple and separate columns for each second
of the interaction (e.g. `blmnwh.6`, `blmnwh.7`, ...). This section
reshapes that into a single long-format table (one row per
couple-second), recodes the dataset's missing-value placeholder to `NA`,
and then splits the negative- and positive-discussion variables into
their own person-level long datasets for plotting and later synchrony
calculation.

**Reshape Wide to Long**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Transform data wide to long
BL_WH_WidetoLong <- BL_WH %>%
  pivot_longer(
    # Select columns like blmnwh.6, blmnwh.7, etc.
    cols = matches("^[^.]+\\.\\d+$"), 
    
    # Split variable name based on period
    names_to = c(".value", "second"),  
    names_sep = "\\." ) %>%
  
  # Convert second to numeric
  mutate(second = as.numeric(second))
```
:::


**Recode Missing Values**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Select the four warmth variables, second, ID
BL_WH_Long <- BL_WH_WidetoLong %>%
  select(ID, second, blmnwh, blmpwh, blfnwh, blfpwh)

# Set 0 as missing
BL_WH_Long$blmnwh[BL_WH_Long$blmnwh == 0] <- NA
BL_WH_Long$blmpwh[BL_WH_Long$blmpwh == 0] <- NA
BL_WH_Long$blfnwh[BL_WH_Long$blfnwh == 0] <- NA
BL_WH_Long$blfpwh[BL_WH_Long$blfpwh == 0] <- NA

# Preview dataset
knitr::kable(head(BL_WH_Long, 5), caption = "Long Baseline Warmth Data")
```

:::


**Create Negative Interaction Dataset**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Create long format for negative interaction 
##(blmnwh = mom, blfnwh = partner)

BL_WH_Neg_Long <- BL_WH_Long %>%
  select(ID, second, blmnwh, blfnwh) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(blmnwh, blfnwh),
    names_to = "source",
    values_to = "blnwh") %>%
  mutate(
    personF = case_when(
      source == "blmnwh" ~ "mom",        #mom
      source == "blfnwh" ~ "partner" ),  #partner
    personN = case_when(
      source == "blmnwh" ~ 1,    #mom
      source == "blfnwh" ~ 2 ))  #partner 

# Set personF as factor
BL_WH_Neg_Long$personF <- as.factor(BL_WH_Neg_Long$personF)

# Set personN as factor
BL_WH_Neg_Long$personN <- as.numeric(BL_WH_Neg_Long$personN)

# Preview dataset
knitr::kable(head(BL_WH_Neg_Long, 20), caption = "Long Baseline Warmth Negative Interaction Data")
```

**Create Positive Interaction Dataset**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Create long format for positive interaction 
##(blmpwh = mom, blfpwh = partner)

BL_WH_Pos_Long <- BL_WH_Long %>%
  select(ID, second, blmpwh, blfpwh) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(blmpwh, blfpwh),
    names_to = "source",
    values_to = "blpwh") %>%
  mutate(
    personF = case_when(
      source == "blmpwh" ~ "mom",        #mom
      source == "blfpwh" ~ "partner" ),  #partner
    personN = case_when(
      source == "blmpwh" ~ 1,    #mom
      source == "blfpwh" ~ 2 ))  #partner 

# Set personF as factor
BL_WH_Pos_Long$personF <- as.factor(BL_WH_Pos_Long$personF)

# Set personN as factor
BL_WH_Pos_Long$personN <- as.numeric(BL_WH_Pos_Long$personN)

# Preview dataset
knitr::kable(head(BL_WH_Pos_Long, 20), caption = "Long Baseline Warmth Positive Interaction Data")
```

These three long-format datasets (`BL_WH_Long`, `BL_WH_Pos_Long`,
`BL_WH_Neg_Long`) are not re-exported here; the [Baseline Synchrony
Calculation](Baseline-Synchrony_Calculation.qmd) page reads the same
processed data from where it's already saved.

## Panel Plots {#secPanel}

The two figures below show second-by-second warmth trends for the full
sample, split by person (mom vs. partner) and by discussion type
(negative vs. positive). The two figures after that repeat the same
comparison for a representative subset of couples, faceted individually,
so that couple-level variation around the sample trend is visible rather
than smoothed away.

**Warmth During Negative Discussion**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="true" code-summary="figure code"}
fig_blnegative_warmth <- ggplot(data = BL_WH_Neg_Long, aes(second, blnwh, color = personF)) +
  geom_smooth(linewidth = 1.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("mom" = "#CC6677", "partner" = "#88CCEE"), name = "Person") +
  labs(title = "Couple Warmth During Negative Discussion") +
  xlab("Time") +
  ylab("Average Warmth") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 16), axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
        panel.grid = element_blank())
```
:::
